title: Constrained 22-Layer Asymmetric Stack with Gradient Regularization
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining initial thickness perturbations to ±25% of the 120nm quarter-wave baseline while applying smoothness regularization on adjacent layer thickness deltas will improve optimizer convergence stability and increase the best_target_score beyond 0.8691 by preventing extreme optical path discontinuities that trap the search in local minima.
design_principle: Quarter-wave baseline initialization with bounded asymmetric perturbations and thickness gradient smoothing to preserve edge-sharpening asymmetry while maintaining impedance continuity across the stack.
proposed_topology: 22 finite layers: alternating TiO2/SiO2 starting with TiO2 on substrate, terminating with SiO2. Exact sequence: TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2
design_variables: 22 layer thicknesses with bounds 90-150nm for initialization, expanded to 30-250nm for optimization
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds prevent extreme deposition challenges
gradient regularization reduces sensitivity to layer-to-layer thickness errors
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack initialization provides physically motivated starting point for local optimization
Thickness gradient smoothing reduces standing wave field intensity peaks that cause fabrication sensitivity
expected_advantages: Improved convergence stability compared to unconstrained 22-layer optimization
known_risks: Constrained initialization may limit exploration of superior non-quarter-wave configurations
Gradient penalty may suppress beneficial asymmetry needed for sharp band edges
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer TiO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate at 45 degrees incidence. Layer sequence: TiO2|SiO2 alternating, starting with TiO2 adjacent to substrate, terminating with SiO2. Initialize all thicknesses at 120nm with random perturbations bounded to ±25% (90-150nm range). Apply soft penalty on absolute thickness difference between adjacent layers during gradient-based optimization. Wavelength bands: 450-650nm (target high reflectance), 700-1000nm (target high transmittance). Optimize all 22 thicknesses with bounds 30-250nm. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 450-650 nm, 700-1000 nm. soft objectives: high reflectance in 450-650 nm; high transmittance in 700-1000 nm; minimized crosstalk between bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 450-650 nm; reflectance in 700-1000 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 24 layers.
revision_reason: Implemented feedback directives: constrained asymmetric seed perturbations to ±25% of 120nm baseline and added soft penalty on thickness gradient between adjacent layers to stabilize spectral margin during early optimization epochs.
